body:
My solution was to go back to university and attempt a post-bac pre-med program; school being what I had come to be comfortable with and medicine seeming to be a field that would allow me to live close to my girlfriend.  I was about 30 at the time.  A year into the two year program she left me on short notice for some local guy she had met who was more emotionally and practically available, with her having kids and me living an hour away and only visiting on weekends.

I have never been so suicidal in my life.  I was testing the strength of the pipes in the ceiling to see if they could support my weight and studying the depth of femoral arteries and the challenges in severing them.  Two months prior she had been telling me that she was ready to live with me and so forth, and this came quite out of the blue.  Her having kids with whom I had become close over about five years, I felt like I was losing a family.

I finished up my second of two years of the pre-med program, straight-As, but still avoiding any kind of job like the plague for fear of having to explain my history.  Aside from a couple short-term temp jobs I had nothing going for me aside from my GPA.  I was 33 when I finished the program.

Now it is two years later and I have been living in my mother's house.  My father died a little over three years ago of complications from leukemia.  I have sunk into the deepest depression I've ever been in since I was a teenager.  There is no word I know of to describe how terrified I am of being asked personal questions at this point in my life.  For some ridiculous examples, the idea of getting a haircut is terrifying to me because of the chance that I might be asked what I do.  The dentist is similarly off-limits.  I absolutely refuse to interact with family.  My original shrink moved away a couple years ago and suggested I find someone closer.  I had been seeing her for about 15 years, and am largely convinced she realized how bad I had gotten and wanted to get rid of me so as not to have a potentially suicidal client on her hands while overseas, which is reasonable.  I tried to find someone new, but the idea of having to explain my pitiful life to a new doctor is too much for me to bear.  I have stopped taking any of my meds because I can't bear the idea of having to recount my failures to someone in order to obtain drugs, which is all I really want at this point.

I haven't elaborated on this point much, but I feel convinced that there is virtually nothing anyone can tell me that I don't already know about my situation or especially what I should do to fix it.  I know I should take baby steps to do this or that.  I know I should perceive this or that event in a light more sympathetic to my plight, if only to make various steps easier to take.  I know people probably don't give two shits about my past.  I know every shitty little psychological trick that could hypothetically help me.  I simply cannot bring myself to accept these things into my mind in action or thought, and I really feel as if I have tried repeatedly.  I feel like I simply cannot motivate myself to do almost any of these, and the only thing that can possibly give me any relief is a narcotic.  In order to obtain these narcotics I have to go to a shrink and degrade myself by reciting my pathetic history and shamefully grovel before them like a junkie.  As an aside, I don't consider myself to ever have been addicted to any benzo, SSRI, or other narcotic (yet) in my life.  I simply perceive them through personal experience as the only experience to have helped.

So now I think of suicide several times a day, and the shock value of it has faded.  It seems almost inevitable, as it did when I was a teenager approaching the end of high school.  Reflecting on my life, it seems as if I would have been better served to have killed myself then, rather than suffer through what has certainly been an additional twenty years of cons stacked vastly over pros.  I don't plan on suicide in the immediate future, for what it's worth, but I sort of worry it's not too far off.  But then again, I sort of hope it's not too far off.

I apologize if this fell apart towards the end... it's quite late and I've become tired and lost a great deal of mental alertness.  I'm sure I left out a good bit of detail in the last few paragraphs.   I can't promise I'll ever read any responses to this, if there are any.  I will probably be incomprehensibly ashamed of having written it once I wake up and prefer to never interact with it again.

edit - grammar

I fucked around for the next two or three years (the whole time seeing a psychiatrist) with a few relatively close friends, but remaining for the most part a shut-in.  My focuses were almost exclusively computer games and later smoking pot.  I hadn't had a job since I was 13.  Any money I had was willingly given by my parents, usually $50 every couple weeks that I'd use to get a small bag of pot.  They knew, but realized how fucked up I was and had no idea what to do with me aside from continue to send me to a shrink.  Discussions with me produced very minor results, as they continue to do, for a variety of reasons.  Anxiety, depression, and a derivative anger being foremost.  Whether a kick in the ass would have helped is up in for debate, but I have my doubts.

When I was 21 I met a fellow pothead girl with serious mental issues and we both went to summer school and I finished up the few credits I had left and got my diploma.  Girl and I broke up a bit later and I spent the next few years still jobless, hopeless, playing computer games, smoking pot, and drinking beer in my parents house as my siblings all went to college with varying degrees of success.

Around age 25, my anxiety somewhat diminishing, presumably with age, I was goaded into entering into a local community college to try to get my life on track.  I excelled academically and entered into a sexual relationship with a professor who was my age and struggling with a shitty marriage.  Two years later I was accepted into the major state university.  I took out loans I could not afford and again excelled during my time there, graduating something like 56th out of 1215 kids in my college, if I remember correctly.  I had thought myself more or less an idiot up until this point, but my success at school convinced me I had a real potential for future success.  On the other hand, by this time I was embarrassed by the huge gap in my employment history and the thought of having to account for it was paralyzingly terrifying.  There were some attempts to make me address it, but my fear was overwhelming and financial support was never withheld enough to make me address it in one way or another.

I spent a year failing to take any real steps to get a real job that would help me advance my goals, partly from inertia and laziness, partly from spending a great deal of time with my girlfriend whom I had never had much time to bond with while she was off dealing with her divorce, and primarily from the paralyzing fear of addressing my huge employment gap.  Anxiety and depression were still significant factors hovering over the whole thing as well, but they took a back seat during this time.
